PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The project is for the construction of a new groundwater supply well and wellhouse for the Village's public water distribution system. There will be a drilling rig needed as part of the construction of 1 test well and the 3 surrounding observation wells. During construction  a drilling rig may be as tall as approximately 40' above the site elevation. For the observation wells  the drill rig will be up for approximately 2 days and will not be taken down until construction is finished. For the Test Well  a drill rig and a crane will be up for approximately 2 weeks and will not be taken down until construction is complete.  A crane will come back to the Test Well approximately 3 months after construction of the Wells are complete  in order to install the Test Well Pump. The crane similarly will be approximately 40' tall and could be up for approximately 5 days before it is taken down. We intend to put the project out to public bid in January 2025  and construction may span over approximately 4-6 months. There will be initial construction early in the project  then approximately 3 months later the crane will come back to the site and finish the project.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: PRPA has plans to construct a new cruise terminal at #4 Hog Island Road along the Delaware River.  The site has an existing pier that can provide access to a cruise ship for embarking and departing of passengers  luggage  and supplies.  The project scope / basis of design includes a new 48 000 square foot cruise terminal building and site development for the following: a drop-off areas for buses  Taxis  Ubers  a 300 000 square foot parking lot  widening of the roads  and covered islands for car pick-up.  The new cruise terminal building approximately 578 feet long x 83 feet wide  and is proposed to be located directly adjacent to the pier.  Site demolition will be limited existing buildings and accessory structures and existing railroad ties than are in conflict with the proposed building footprint  drop off lane and incoming bus parking areas.The cruise terminal building construction is proposed to be an insulated fabric exterior membrane attached to a pre-engineered steel structure.  The building steel columns would be supported and anchored to a structural concrete slab and foundation.  The proposed building foundation system includes concrete spread footings  perimeter grade walls with continuous footings  and interior floor slabs with control joints.  The finished floor of the terminal building will be set equal to the top of the adjacent dock  which is approximately 3’-0” above final grade.   The cruise terminal building will include mechanical heating  ventilation  air conditioning (HVAC)  plumbing  fire protection  and electrical components.  The attached Concept Sketch depicts the proposed building location on the site layout and overall project scope of work.  The sketch was developed by Bowman Consulting Group  who is the engineering firm restoring the pier.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The site is located at #4 Hog Island Road  Philadelphia  PA and is currently owned by Energy Transfer.  There is a paved access road off Fort Mifflin Road / Hog Island Road to access the site. The majority of the site is abandoned  with four buildings either unoccupied or not-in-use. The site is paved  relatively flat  and there are some wetlands adjacent to the vegetated  undeveloped areas.  There are signs of existing utilities below the vegetated areas. The site provides access to an existing pier  over 1 000 feet in length  located on the Delaware River.  There are adjacent structures / buildings within a mile radius such as the the Philadelphia International Airport  the UPS Cargo Building  Menzies Aviation PHL Fuel Facility and Sunoco Logistics.  The site is located south of the Philadelphia International Airport.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The New York City School Construction Authority (SCA) is proposing the construction of a new educational facility located at 146-50 Reeves Avenue  Queens  NY  to serve as an annex to the existing John Bowne High School. The project site is situated in a developed urban area and falls within FAA Part 77 notification criteria due to its proximity to navigable airspace associated with LaGuardia Airport.nnThe project has undergone preliminary evaluation under FAA Study No. 2024-AEA-396-OE and was issued a Determination of No Hazard to Air Navigation on February 12  2024  with the condition that Form 7460-2 (Part 2) be submitted within 5 days of reaching maximum height.nnThis proposal is being submitted in accordance with FAA regulations to ensure continued compliance with 14 CFR Part 77 and to notify the FAA of anticipated construction activity on site.

It will serve as an annex to the existing school and is situated in a primarily residential and institutional area. The project site lies approximately 0.9 miles southwest of LaGuardia Airport's outer airspace boundaries and is surrounded by other mid-rise buildings and community structures. The project has been reviewed under FAA aeronautical study 2024-AEA-396-OE and determined to present no hazard to air navigation.

LOCATION DESCRIPTION: Dominion is proposing to rebuild 3 miles of existing Line 27  115 kV overhead electric transmission line  in the Shore Drive area of Virginia Beach  Virginia. Proposed Structures 72  52  and 1 are in the vicinity of existing towers/structures OAS 51-001439  OAS 51-068723  and OAS 51-068072  respectively. All proposed structures for this filing are located at minimum 1.0 miles from Naval Air Station Oceana NTU.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: Since the MCCL property is located adjacent to the Leesburg Executive Airport  no building or structure constructed on the property shall exceed height limits imposed by FAA or Zoning Ordinance  whichever is more restrictive. The proposed design demonstrates that the height of the building has compliance with FAA requirements  does not impact primary or secondary approach surface to Leesburg Executive Airport  and does not create a hazard to air navigation. The FAA documentation which was obtained for study is confirming compliance to the latest guideline.nThe FAA proposed guideline dictates that buildings or structures less than 1000 feet from end of a runway shall not exceed 160 feet in height. The MCCL project is located more than 1000 feet from the Leesburg Executive Airport's end of runway and shall not impact the 160 feet height restriction. The top of the proposed minaretes is at 65 feet above finished grading which makes the structure within the limitation.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The MCCL project is located at 19838 Sycolin Road  Leesburg  Virginia 20175 close to the Leesburg Airport. The proposed MCCL building will be located 920 feet from end of Leesburg Airport runway.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This project proposes to replace the existing steel through truss bridge carrying NY-33A (Chili Avenue) over the Erie Canal between the City of Rochester and the Town of Gates in Monroe County. A new widened and slightly longer steel through truss bridge will serve the purpose ofnenhancing the transportation facilities for vehicular traffic and create improved accommodations for bicyclists and pedestrians in the Immediate area. The project will require the complete closure of the bridge for anticipated 18-month period during which a signed off-site detour willnbe provided for vehicular traffic. Bicycle and pedestrian accommodations along NY-33A will be maintained throughout the project via a temporary pedestrian bridge located just north of the bridge crossing. In addition  the Erie Canalway Trail  located just west of the bridge  will remain accessible during construction. This bridge crossing serves as a gateway to the City of Rochester from the nearby 1-390 and its western suburbs. The design of the new bridge will take into consideration the historic significance of the Erie Canal.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: NY-33A (Chili Avenue) over the Erie Canal between the City of Rochester and the Town of Gates in Monroe County.nnNY-33A is an approximate 17-mile east-west state highway traversing through the western reaches of Monroe County  beginning in the City of Rochester and extending westerly into Genesee County. It is comprised of two unique common names throughout its length. In Monroe County  NY-33A is commonly referred to as Chili Avenue  the name it retains as it passes through the project location on its way into the City of Rochester.n•nBeginning approximately one mile west of the project location and moving eastward  NY-33A passes through a mostly residential area before entering a more commercialized  retail district.nAt this point  the route meets 1-390 at Exit 19 and intersects Buell Road (CR 162)  which links NY-33A to the Frederick Douglas - Greater Rochester International Airport  one half-mile to the south. Continuing eastward  NY-33A immediately crosses the historic Erie Canal on a 148-foot steel-through truss bridge and enters the City of Rochester  at which point maintenance of NY-n33A shifts from the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT) to the City of Rochester. Immediately east of the Erie Canal crossing  the route intersects with Cairn Street  and continues east as it passes under the Rochester and Southern Railroad. The surroundings become significantly more residential east of the railroad as the route heads eastward towardndowntown Rochester.n• The project location is in an urban area.n• Land use in the immediate area is mixed-use commercial and residential.n• Pedestrian travel primarily consists of residents commuting for work and pleasure tonand from the commercial areas that include restaurants and shops.n• The Erie Canal and the Canalway Trail are recreational and historic resources.n• Regional Transit Service (RTS} buses use this bridge for several daily routes.n• This bridge is a contributing element of the Historic Erie Canal.n• State and local politicians may be interested In this project because of its historic significance and Its location along a busy corridor near the Frederick Douglass Greater Rochester International Airport. Nearby residents and those commuting through the area may contact elected officials with concerns.n• Project Environmental Justice Screening indicates significant low income and minority populations.nAirport is 1 Mile south of the bridge location
